seoTitle: Samsung Free Fire Sensitivity for 2GB to 16GB Phones
seoDescription: How to set Free Fire sensitivity on a Samsung Galaxy, from a 2GB A06 to a 16GB S26 Ultra, with a 4GB headshot start and a straight answer on which Galaxy is worth buying.

content.html:
Samsung sensitivity depends on the phone in your hand

One code does not fit every Galaxy. A 4GB Galaxy A14 drops frames in a long match, so the swipe shows up a little late and the crosshair needs a higher number to reach the head. An S25 Ultra or S26 Ultra is already quick. Paste that same high number in and the aim skips past the player you were tracking.

Use the calculator above. Choose your Samsung model and the RAM that is actually in the phone. For the first try, leave the rest alone: Auto Custom, a phone about six months old, 60 FPS, two fingers, Rusher, foregrip on. Change one setting after you have felt that start. Not five.

Start from the RAM you have

The cheaper Galaxies people still play on — A06, A12, A14, A15, A17 5G, F17 5G — belong on the 2GB, 3GB and 4GB rows. Smoother phones such as the A26 5G, A34 5G, A35 5G and A36 5G belong on 6GB and 8GB. The S25 Ultra and S26 Ultra belong on 12GB and 16GB.

Two and three gigabytes land on the same start. Twelve and sixteen do too. The boost only steps at 4GB, then 6GB, then 8GB, then 12GB. On the cheaper phones General often sits on 200, because Free Fire will not go past 200. Look at the red dot and the scopes. That is where a 2GB phone and a 4GB phone actually separate.

If the drag feels nervous, lower the red dot before you touch General. If the gun never climbs to the chest, add a little to the red dot and leave the sniper scope until you are actually holding a sniper.

Headshots on a 4GB Galaxy

Switch Player Role to Precision aim when you want a headshot setup on 4GB. This fits the phones most people still bring into Free Fire: Galaxy A06, A12, A14, A14 5G, A15, A17 5G and F17 5G.

  • General: 200
  • Red Dot: 191
  • 2X Scope: 155
  • 4X Scope: 151
  • Sniper Scope: 95
  • Free Look: 145
  • Fire Button Size: 41%

The fire button comes down to 41% so your thumb is not sitting on the head you are trying to hit. Take an MP40 into the training ground before you queue. Up close, pull in a short curve. At mid range, pull straight and stop at the chin. If the crosshair jumps over the head, take five off the red dot and shoot the same bot again. Ten quiet minutes will tell you more than another list.

The Galaxy models players ask for by name

The RAM in the phone decides the number. The model name does not override it. If your A35 has 6GB instead of 8GB, use the 6GB row.

A14, A14 5G, A15, A06, A12, A17 5G and F17 5G

Treat these as one group at 4GB. General 200, red dot 177, 2x 155, 4x 151, sniper 95, free look 159, fire button 45%. An A14 5G does not need a different code from an A14. An A06 or A12 with only 2GB or 3GB moves the red dot to 181 and free look to 164. General stays on the cap either way.

A34 5G and A26 5G

These track better than an A14, so the sensitivity comes down with them. At 6GB: General 186, red dot 159, 2x 140, 4x 136, sniper 85, free look 144, fire button 42%. On an 8GB unit, General lands on 183 and the red dot on 156. Leave it there for a few matches before you push it back up. A higher number on a phone that already tracks well is how sprays get loose.

A35 5G and A36 5G

At 8GB the start is General 183, red dot 156, 2x 137, 4x 133, sniper 84, free look 141, fire button 42%. A 6GB version of the same phone uses the A34 numbers above. Both of these can hold 60 FPS without the sensitivity having to compensate the way a 4GB phone does.

Which Samsung is worth buying for Free Fire

Buy the phone for a steady frame rate. A thumbnail that calls something the best gaming phone for Free Fire is not a spec sheet. On Samsung, the choice usually falls into three groups.

  • If the budget reaches a flagship: Galaxy S26 Ultra, S25 Ultra, S24 Ultra, Z Fold7 or Z Flip7. At 12GB or 16GB the start is General 170, red dot 145, 2x 127, 4x 124, sniper 78, free look 131. Keep it lower than an A-series. The screen is already fast, and 90 or 120 FPS makes a high General feel slippery.
  • If you want the phone you can play on every day: Galaxy A56 5G, A55 5G, A36 5G, A35 5G, M56 5G or F56 5G with 8GB. General 183 and red dot 156 is enough. This is the range where Free Fire stays comfortable without the phone heating your hand every match.
  • If you are staying on a cheaper Galaxy: A17 5G, F17 5G, A15 5G, A14 5G or M15 5G. Use the 4GB setup, set graphics to Smooth, and close WhatsApp and the browser before you drop. Sensitivity cannot fix a phone that has run out of memory.

Five Samsung phones under ₹10,000 that can run Free Fire

Ten thousand rupees does not buy a Samsung made for Free Fire. It buys a phone that can finish a match if graphics stay on Smooth and the other apps are closed. The prices here are what these models were selling for in India in late October 2026. They shift every week, so read the listing before you pay.

Inside this budget, a 90Hz screen beats a cheaper 60Hz screen. The chip matters more than whether the box says M, F or A.

Galaxy M14 (4G)

Around ₹8,500. Snapdragon 680, a 90Hz screen, and 4GB of RAM. If Free Fire is the reason you are shopping, start here. Turning around feels less sticky than it does on the Helio phones below. In the calculator, pick Samsung Galaxy M14 and the 4GB row: General 200, red dot 177, 2x 155, 4x 151, sniper 95, free look 159.

Galaxy F14 (4G)

Around ₹8,800. The same class of phone, with a Snapdragon 680 and a 90Hz panel. Take this when the M14 is gone. Do not step up to the 5G M14 or F14 unless the price is still under ten thousand. The sensitivity start does not change.

Galaxy F05

Around ₹6,500. Helio G85, a 60Hz screen, 4GB, and a 5,000mAh battery. It opens Free Fire. It does not feel like the M14 once a fight gets busy. Stay at 60 FPS, keep graphics on Smooth, and use that same 4GB row. If the drag stutters, the phone has run out of memory.

Galaxy M05

Around ₹6,700. This is the F05 sold through Samsung's other shop. Same chip, same 60Hz panel, same 4GB. Buy whichever one is actually in stock. No sensitivity code makes an M05 play like an M14.

Galaxy A05

Around ₹7,800. Helio G85 again, 60Hz, and usually easier to find at a local counter than the F-series. Reasonable as a first phone. A poor swap if you already have one of the 90Hz models and someone calls this an upgrade.

Leave out any under-₹10,000 list that quietly adds an M06, F06 or A06 5G. Those have the stronger Dimensity chip, and in October 2026 they were mostly priced above this budget. If a real sale puts one of them under ten thousand, take that over every phone above.

Copy one row, then stop changing it

Open Free Fire, open sensitivity, and copy only the row that matches your RAM. That habit covers the Galaxy phones on this page, from last year's A-series through the S25 and S26. Play training until the drag stops surprising you. If a friend on another brand sends you their code, leave it. Their screen is not your screen.
